The enterprise AI war just shifted from model capability to execution control.

At Dreamforce this week, Salesforce introduced AIforce and Koa — a deliberate architectural split that separates the AI interface layer from the trusted enterprise context and execution layer. Koa adds CRM-specific reasoning through a Salesforce-controlled model, meaning the intelligence is now governed by the platform vendor, not outsourced to a frontier lab.

This is not a feature announcement. It is an architectural declaration. Salesforce is signaling that enterprise AI value will accrue not to whoever has the best model, but to whoever controls the context layer — the customer data, the business logic, the workflow execution.

HubSpot made a parallel move the same week with Growth Context, rebuilding Breeze and its Smart CRM to continuously assemble customer context and activate it across marketing, sales, and service. Mistral is echoing the same thesis: enterprise AI will be about control, not just intelligence.

For CEOs and CTOs, the strategic implication is direct. If your AI strategy is built on plugging a general-purpose LLM into your stack, you are ceding your most valuable asset — proprietary business context — to a vendor's execution layer. The winners will be organizations that own their context architecture and select AI execution layers accordingly.
